# CastleEarly

> CastleEarly (castleearly.com) is a free chess website for beginners and improving players. Visitors can play chess in the browser against the computer (Easy, Medium, Hard, or Master powered by Stockfish 19 lite) or a friend, analyze their Chess.com and Lichess games free with Stockfish, and learn the rules, 25 openings, the classic opening traps, 28 tactics and the basic endgames on interactive boards. No sign-up is needed.

Every opening line and puzzle on the site is checked move by move with a chess engine. Lessons are written in plain English by the CastleEarly team. CastleEarly is independent and not affiliated with Chess.com or Lichess.

## Tools
- [Play Chess Online Free vs Computer or a Friend](https://castleearly.com/): Play chess free against the computer (Easy to Master/Stockfish) or a friend, then get free Stockfish analysis of every move. No sign-up, no download.
- [Free Chess Analysis with Stockfish](https://castleearly.com/analysis/): Free chess analysis and game review with Stockfish: import your Chess.com or Lichess games or paste a PGN and see accuracy, blunders and best moves. No sign-up.

## Learn the rules
- [How to Play Chess: Rules for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/learn/): Learn how to play chess step by step: the goal, the board, how each piece moves, check, checkmate, stalemate and draws. Free interactive boards for beginners.
- [How to Set Up a Chess Board (Easy Tricks)](https://castleearly.com/learn/chess-board-setup/): How to set up a chess board correctly: which way the board goes, where each piece goes, and easy tricks to remember the king and queen squares.
- [How Chess Pieces Move (with Piece Values)](https://castleearly.com/learn/how-chess-pieces-move/): How each chess piece moves, explained simply with an interactive board for each one: king, queen, rook, bishop, knight and pawn, plus what each piece is worth.
- [3 Special Moves in Chess: Castling, En Passant, Promotion](https://castleearly.com/learn/special-moves/): Learn the three special moves in chess: castling, en passant and pawn promotion. Simple rules, common questions and an interactive board for each.
- [Chess Notation Explained: Read and Write Moves](https://castleearly.com/learn/chess-notation/): Chess notation explained simply: square names, piece letters, captures, check, checkmate, castling and promotion, with an interactive example game.
- [Stalemate in Chess: Rules, Examples and How to Avoid It](https://castleearly.com/learn/stalemate/): Stalemate in chess is a draw: the player to move has no legal move but isn't in check. The rule, what causes it, clear examples and how to avoid it.
- [Zugzwang in Chess: Meaning, Examples and How to Use It](https://castleearly.com/learn/zugzwang/): Zugzwang means every move you can make worsens your position. The meaning, the trébuchet, the opposition, triangulation and practice positions.
- [En Passant in Chess: Rules and Examples](https://castleearly.com/learn/en-passant/): En passant is a special pawn capture: take a pawn that moved two squares past yours, on the very next move only. Rules, examples and practice.
- [Smothered Mate in Chess: Pattern, Examples and Traps](https://castleearly.com/learn/smothered-mate/): A smothered mate is checkmate by a knight when the king is boxed in by its own pieces. Learn the pattern, Philidor's legacy, three opening traps and practice.
- [Castling in Chess: Rules, How to Do It and When You Can't](https://castleearly.com/learn/castling/): Castling moves your king two squares toward a rook, and the rook jumps over it. Learn the rules, kingside vs queenside, and every case where you can't castle.
- [Pawn Promotion in Chess: Rules, Examples and FAQs](https://castleearly.com/learn/pawn-promotion/): When a pawn reaches the last rank it must promote to a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Learn the promotion rules, multiple queens, underpromotion and notation.
- [Draw in Chess: All 5 Ways a Game Can End in a Draw](https://castleearly.com/learn/chess-draw-rules/): A chess game is drawn by stalemate, threefold repetition, the 50-move rule, insufficient material or agreement. Each draw rule explained with examples.
- [Checkmate Patterns: 10 Mates Every Player Should Know](https://castleearly.com/learn/checkmate-patterns/): Learn 10 essential checkmate patterns with a free puzzle for each: back-rank, ladder, smothered, Arabian, Anastasia's, Boden's, epaulette, opera mate and more.

## Openings
- [Chess Openings for Beginners: White and Black](https://castleearly.com/openings/): A library of 25 chess openings for White and Black plus the most common opening traps, each with an interactive board, plans and a practice mode.
- [Best Chess Openings for Beginners (White and Black)](https://castleearly.com/openings/best-chess-openings-for-beginners/): The best chess openings for beginners, for White and Black: the best first moves, a comparison table, why each opening works and free interactive lessons.
- [Chess Opening Quiz: Which Opening Suits You?](https://castleearly.com/openings/which-opening-suits-you/): Free chess opening quiz: answer five quick questions about your style and level and find which openings you should play as White and as Black.
- [Caro-Kann Defense: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/caro-kann-defense/): Learn the Caro-Kann Defense (1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5) move by move: the Classical and Advance variations, Black's plans, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [English Opening (1.c4): Chess Moves, Plans and Variations](https://castleearly.com/openings/english-opening/): The English Opening in chess starts 1.c4. Main lines (Reversed Sicilian, Symmetrical, Anglo-Indian, Agincourt), the Botvinnik system for White, how Black should reply, and a free interactive board.
- [Four Knights Game: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/four-knights-game/): Learn the Four Knights Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6) move by move: the Spanish and Scotch versions, plans, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [French Defense: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/french-defense/): Learn the French Defense (1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5) move by move: the Advance and Classical variations, Black's plans, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [Fried Liver Attack: Moves, Traps and Defense](https://castleearly.com/openings/fried-liver-attack/): Learn the Fried Liver Attack (4.Ng5 and 6.Nxf7) move by move: the knight sacrifice, Black's correct 5...Na5 defense, the Traxler and a free practice board.
- [Italian Game: Moves, Plans and Traps](https://castleearly.com/openings/italian-game/): Learn the Italian Game chess opening (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4) move by move. Main ideas, plans for White and Black, common traps, and a board to practice on.
- [King's Indian Defense: Beginner's Guide](https://castleearly.com/openings/kings-indian-defense/): Learn the King's Indian Defense (1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6) move by move: the Classical main line, a setup against the London, Black's plans and a practice board.
- [London System: Setup and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/london-system/): Learn the London System chess opening (1.d4 and 2.Bf4) step by step. The setup, the plans, how to handle ...Qb6 and ...Bd6, and a free board to practice on.
- [Nimzo-Indian Defense: Beginner's Guide](https://castleearly.com/openings/nimzo-indian-defense/): Learn the Nimzo-Indian Defense (1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4) move by move: the Rubinstein and Classical lines, Black's plans and a free practice board.
- [Petrov Defense: Moves, Plans and the Key Trap](https://castleearly.com/openings/petrov-defense/): Learn the Petrov Defense (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6) move by move: the main line, the trap every Black player must avoid, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [Queen's Gambit: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/queens-gambit/): Learn the Queen's Gambit (1.d4 d5 2.c4) move by move: the Declined and Accepted lines, plans for White, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [Queen's Gambit Declined: Beginner's Guide](https://castleearly.com/openings/queens-gambit-declined/): Learn the Queen's Gambit Declined (1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6) move by move: the Tartakower setup, the Elephant Trap, Black's plans and a free practice board.
- [Ruy Lopez: Moves, Plans and Traps](https://castleearly.com/openings/ruy-lopez/): Learn the Ruy Lopez (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5) move by move: the Closed main line, plans for both sides, the Noah's Ark trap and a free practice board.
- [Scandinavian Defense: Beginner's Guide](https://castleearly.com/openings/scandinavian-defense/): Learn the Scandinavian Defense (1.e4 d5) move by move: the ...Qa5 and ...Qd6 lines, Black's plans, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [Scotch Game: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/scotch-game/): Learn the Scotch Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4) move by move: the main lines, plans for both sides, a classic beginner mistake, and a free practice board.
- [Sicilian Defense: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/sicilian-defense/): Learn the Sicilian Defense (1.e4 c5) move by move: the Najdorf main line, how to face the Alapin, plans for both sides and a free practice board.
- [Slav Defense: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/slav-defense/): Learn the Slav Defense (1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6) move by move: the main line, the Exchange Slav, Black's plans, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [Vienna Game: Moves and Plans for Beginners](https://castleearly.com/openings/vienna-game/): Learn the Vienna Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nc3) and the Vienna Gambit move by move, with plans for both sides, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [King's Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.f4): Moves, Ideas and Traps](https://castleearly.com/openings/kings-gambit/): Learn the King's Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.f4) move by move: accepted and declined lines, White's attacking plans, the ...Qh4+ danger and a free practice board.
- [Danish Gambit: Moves, Traps and How to Defend It](https://castleearly.com/openings/danish-gambit/): Learn the Danish Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3) move by move: the two-pawn sacrifice, White's attack, Black's best defenses and a free practice board.
- [Evans Gambit (4.b4): Moves, Plans and Main Lines](https://castleearly.com/openings/evans-gambit/): Learn the Evans Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.b4) move by move: why White gives the b-pawn, the main lines, Black's defenses and a free practice board.
- [Smith-Morra Gambit: Moves, Traps and Main Lines](https://castleearly.com/openings/smith-morra-gambit/): Learn the Smith-Morra Gambit (1.e4 c5 2.d4 cxd4 3.c3) move by move: White's setup, the main lines, the Siberian Trap and a free practice board.
- [Queen's Gambit Accepted: Moves, Plans and Traps](https://castleearly.com/openings/queens-gambit-accepted/): Learn the Queen's Gambit Accepted (1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4) move by move: why Black takes the pawn, the main line, the ...b5 trap to avoid and a free practice board.
- [Pirc Defense (1.e4 d6): Moves, Plans and Main Lines](https://castleearly.com/openings/pirc-defense/): Learn the Pirc Defense (1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6) move by move: Black's setup and pawn breaks, the Austrian Attack, common mistakes and a free practice board.
- [Dutch Defense (1.d4 f5): Stonewall, Leningrad and Traps](https://castleearly.com/openings/dutch-defense/): Learn the Dutch Defense (1.d4 f5) move by move: the Stonewall, Leningrad and Classical setups, Black's kingside plans, a trap to avoid and a free practice board.

## Opening traps
- [Scholar's Mate (4-Move Checkmate): How to Do It and Stop It](https://castleearly.com/openings/scholars-mate/): Scholar's Mate is the 4-move checkmate: 1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 Nc6 3.Qh5 Nf6?? 4.Qxf7#. Learn every move order, how to stop it with ...g6, and how to punish the early queen (...Nd4!), plus Scholar's Mate for Black.
- [Fool's Mate: the Fastest Checkmate in Chess](https://castleearly.com/openings/fools-mate/): Fool's Mate is the fastest checkmate in chess: 1.f3 e5 2.g4?? Qh4#. See why it works, every version of it, and the simple rule that keeps you safe.
- [Englund Gambit (1.d4 e5): the Trap and the Best Response](https://castleearly.com/openings/englund-gambit/): The Englund Gambit (1.d4 e5) move by move: the famous ...Qc1# trap, how to play it as Black, the best response for White, and a free practice board.
- [Stafford Gambit: Traps and How to Refute It](https://castleearly.com/openings/stafford-gambit/): Learn the Stafford Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6) move by move: its two deadliest traps, how White should refute it, and a free practice board.

## Tactics and endgames
- [Chess Tactics: 28 Patterns with Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/): Learn 28 chess tactics with free interactive puzzles: forks, pins, skewers, deflection, interference, windmill, Greek gift, zugzwang and more.
- [Basic Chess Endgames: Practice Checkmates](https://castleearly.com/endgames/): Learn the basic chess checkmates with king and queen, king and rook, two rooks and king and pawn. Practice each one against the computer for free.
- [King and Queen Checkmate: How to Mate Step by Step](https://castleearly.com/endgames/king-and-queen-checkmate/): Learn how to checkmate with a king and queen against a lone king: the box method in four steps, how to avoid stalemate, and a free practice board.
- [King and Rook Checkmate: How to Mate Step by Step](https://castleearly.com/endgames/king-and-rook-checkmate/): Learn how to checkmate with a king and rook against a lone king: cut the king off, use the opposition and the waiting move, and practice on a free board.

## Individual tactics
- [Hanging Pieces in Chess: How to Spot and Win Them](https://castleearly.com/tactics/hanging-piece/): A hanging piece is attacked and not defended. Learn how to spot hanging pieces, stop leaving your own en prise, and practice with free puzzles.
- [Fork in Chess: What It Is, Examples and Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/fork/): A fork in chess is one piece attacking two or more enemy pieces at the same time. Learn knight, pawn and queen forks and practice with free puzzles.
- [Pin in Chess: Absolute and Relative Pins Explained](https://castleearly.com/tactics/pin/): A pin in chess stops a piece from moving because a more valuable piece stands behind it. Learn absolute and relative pins, how to break them, and practice.
- [Skewer in Chess: Definition, Examples and Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/skewer/): A skewer attacks a valuable piece that must move, exposing the piece behind it. Learn how skewers work, how they differ from pins, and practice free.
- [Trapped Piece in Chess: How to Trap and Win Pieces](https://castleearly.com/tactics/trapped-piece/): A piece is trapped when it is attacked and has no safe square. Learn the classic bishop, knight and queen traps and practice with free puzzles.
- [Discovered Attack in Chess: Examples and Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/discovered-attack/): A discovered attack uncovers an attack from the piece behind when another piece moves away. Learn discovered checks and practice with free puzzles.
- [Back-Rank Mate in Chess: How It Works and How to Stop It](https://castleearly.com/tactics/back-rank-mate/): A back-rank mate is checkmate by a rook or queen on the last rank against a king trapped by its own pawns. Learn the pattern, how to stop it, and practice.
- [Battery in Chess: Lining Up Pieces to Attack](https://castleearly.com/tactics/battery/): A battery is two or more pieces lined up on a file, rank or diagonal. Learn queen and bishop batteries, doubled rooks and Alekhine's gun, with puzzles.
- [Ladder Mate: Checkmate with Two Rooks, Step by Step](https://castleearly.com/tactics/ladder-mate/): The ladder mate uses two rooks, or a rook and queen, to push the king to the edge one rank at a time. Learn the method step by step and practice it.
- [Removing the Defender in Chess: Examples and Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/removing-the-defender/): Removing the defender means capturing or driving off the piece that protects your target. Learn how to spot it and practice with free puzzles.
- [Deflection in Chess: Definition, Examples and Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/deflection/): Deflection forces a defending piece to leave its post, so the square or piece it guarded falls. Learn the pattern and practice with free puzzles.
- [Overloading in Chess: The Overworked Piece](https://castleearly.com/tactics/overloading/): An overloaded piece defends two things at once and can't do both. Learn to spot overworked defenders and practice with free puzzles.
- [Decoy in Chess: Luring a Piece to a Bad Square](https://castleearly.com/tactics/decoy/): A decoy sacrifice lures the king or another piece onto a square where a fork, pin or mate is waiting. Learn the pattern and practice with free puzzles.
- [X-Ray Attack in Chess: Attacking Through a Piece](https://castleearly.com/tactics/x-ray/): An x-ray is a rook, bishop or queen acting through another piece on the same line. Learn x-ray attacks and x-ray defense, with free puzzles.
- [Double Check in Chess: Rules, Examples and Puzzles](https://castleearly.com/tactics/double-check/): In a double check two pieces give check at once, so the king must move. Learn how double checks happen, why they are so strong, and practice free.
- [Zwischenzug in Chess: The In-Between Move Explained](https://castleearly.com/tactics/zwischenzug/): A zwischenzug is a surprise in-between move played before the expected recapture. Learn the meaning, pronunciation and examples, with free puzzles.
- [Desperado in Chess: Selling a Doomed Piece Dearly](https://castleearly.com/tactics/desperado/): A desperado is a piece that is about to be lost and captures whatever it can first. Learn when to use it and practice with free puzzles.
- [Interference in Chess: Cutting a Defender's Line](https://castleearly.com/tactics/interference/): Interference places a piece on the line between an enemy defender and what it guards. Learn how the tactic works and practice with a free puzzle.
- [Clearance Sacrifice in Chess: Clearing a Square or Line](https://castleearly.com/tactics/clearance/): A clearance sacrifice moves your own piece off a square or line so another piece can use it. Learn the pattern and practice with free puzzles.
- [Windmill in Chess: The See-Saw Tactic Explained](https://castleearly.com/tactics/windmill/): A windmill is a series of discovered checks where a rook captures piece after piece. Learn how it works, see Torre vs Lasker, and practice free.
- [Greek Gift Sacrifice: The Bxh7+ Attack Explained](https://castleearly.com/tactics/greek-gift/): The Greek gift is the classic bishop sacrifice Bxh7+ against a castled king. Learn the conditions that make it work, the main lines, and practice it.
- [Pawn Breakthrough: The 3 vs 3 Sacrifice Explained](https://castleearly.com/tactics/pawn-breakthrough/): A pawn breakthrough sacrifices pawns to force one through to promotion. Learn the classic three against three breakthrough and practice it free.
- [Underpromotion in Chess: When Not to Take a Queen](https://castleearly.com/tactics/underpromotion/): Underpromotion is promoting a pawn to a knight, rook or bishop instead of a queen. Learn when and why to do it, with examples and free puzzles.
- [Perpetual Check in Chess: How to Force a Draw](https://castleearly.com/tactics/perpetual-check/): Perpetual check is a series of checks the king can't escape, which forces a draw. Learn how it works under the rules and practice with a free puzzle.
